generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent primary-key value; with probability ~0.01 emit NULL when the column is nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.bigint_fk: Copy an existing parent primary-key value; with probability ~0.01 emit NULL when the column is nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short_code: Uppercase alphanumeric strings of length 2-4 drawn from a pool of ~500 distinct codes; allow near-variants (case changes, one-character edits) for LIKE/equality literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Title-case words of length 3-40; allow near-variants (truncation, case change) for LIKE literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_country: Country names from a pool of ~240 values; allow case variants (e.g. 'China'/'china') and near-variants for LIKE literals.
generic_sampling_rules.real_coordinate: Uniform real in [-180, 180] for longitude-like columns and [-90, 90] for latitude-like columns; 6 decimal places.
generic_sampling_rules.bigint_elevation: Integer in [-1500, 9000] with a long right tail; allow ties at the maximum for LIMIT(1) queries.
generic_sampling_rules.flag_y_n: Value in ('Y','N'); allow lowercase 'y' as a near-variant.
generic_sampling_rules.nullable_text: With probability equal to the column's null_rate emit NULL; otherwise a fresh value from the column's domain.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: 0.3 of text values are fresh; 0.7 are drawn from the existing pool to create duplicates and ties.

per_column_exceptions.targets: Include parent airports with no routes (parent_rows_without_children) and routes with NULL dst_apid/src_apid (child_rows_with_null_fk).
Group sizes 1, 2 and >= 3 when grouped by apid.
Tie at rank 1 for ORDER(COUNT(*), DESC) and ORDER(COUNT(routes.rid), DESC).
At least 2 rows per group with different values; tie at rank 1 for LIMIT(1) on MAX(elevation).
Parent airlines with no routes; routes with NULL alid.
Tie at rank 1 for ORDER(COUNT(routes.rid), DESC) and ORDER(COUNT(*), DESC).
Tie at rank 1 for ORDER(COUNT(*), DESC).
Tie at rank 1 for ORDER(COUNT(routes.rid), DESC).

supporting_evidence.routes.dst_ap: Sample rows 37-45 show dst_ap matching the IATA code of the airport with apid=dst_apid (e.g. rid 37 dst_apid 2990 dst_ap 'KZ').
supporting_evidence.routes.src_ap: Sample rows show src_ap matching the IATA code of the airport with apid=src_apid (e.g. rid 37 src_apid 2965 src_ap 'AER').
supporting_evidence.routes.airline: Sample rows show airline matching the IATA code of the airline with alid (e.g. rid 37 alid 410 airline '2B').
supporting_evidence.airports.x: Statistics show x values like 145.39, -45.42, -51.68, all within [-180,180].
supporting_evidence.airports.y: Statistics show y values like -6.08, 61.16, 64.19, all within [-90,90].
supporting_evidence.airlines.active: Statistics show distinct values 2; sample shows 'Y' and 'N'.
supporting_evidence.routes.codeshare: Statistics show distinct 1 with null_rate 0.784; sample shows 'Y'.

uncertainty: The exact IATA/ICAO code pools are not fully known; near-variants are generated generically. The null_rate for routes.alid is 0.007, so NULL rows are rare but present. The formula routes.dst_ap = airports.iata holds only when the airport has an IATA code; some airports may have empty iata, so the condition is stated.
